Imgur isn't really part of reddit, I don't think using it is "feeding the reddit monster", but to answer your question, http://puush.me is probably the best one I've ever used. You can take screenshots and upload images in seconds just using key bindings, and then the link is automatically copied to my keyboard. I took and uploaded this screenshot in 5 seconds.

Also works with other files too, not just images.

It's ephemeral. It unpredictably deletes your images. Any regular image that's not viewed regularly will get deleted after a few months or so. Are you sure that someone will keep revisiting all your uploaded images, to make sure they don't go away? Will you? The next time you revisit an old imgur link you saved, that image could be gone.
That's only the case with images you submit to the public gallery. Images you just upload to their servers stay there forever.
I'm not sure what you mean by submitting to the public gallery as opposed to uploading to their servers.

When you upload a picture to Imgur, that picture is viewable to you and anyone you send the link to.

When you submit it to the gallery, that picture gets shoved into Imgur's \new feed which allows Imgur's community to comment and vote on it, etc. This is not required to look at the picture and is in fact heavily discouraged unless you actually think it's meaningful content for the average imgur user.

Imgur only removes pictures from the gallery. It'll never delete a picture from their server itself unless you specifically ask them to.

Thanks for the clarification.

It at least definitely used to be the case that imgur did delete images in exactly the way I described above. Not only did I personally encounter this issue, but it was even mentioned in their FAQ.

However, they've since redesigned their site, and now I can't find that FAQ anymore, and I guess it's possible that they've also changed their image retention policy, and that you are now correct.

It is hard to check if you are, because it's hard to check whether imgur still deletes "inactive" images without knowing after exactly how long a time period of zero access images might be deleted. Even if I knew that the length of that time was, say, a year, then in order to prove the point, I'd have to upload an image today, not access it and not tell the URL to anyone (and not submit it to the gallery you mentioned), and then I'd have to wait more than a year and then get back to you.

The truth is, unless somebody has a definite answer straight from the horse's mouth, we just can't know, and it's better to err on the side of security and follow Nyutral's advice and keep local copies.

PS: The Wayback Machine delivers! The grace period used to be six months. I'll better be safe than sorry, so I assume they're still deleting "inactive" images. If you want to prove otherwise, you could indeed do the above experiment. However, the image-may-be-removed-after-that stipulation in the old FAQ is fantastically vague, so even if you did the experiment and your image was kept for six months or even a year of zero access, you still couldn't prove that they delete NO "inactive" images. It's typically very hard to prove a negative.
As for me, if there's anything I think I might want to look at later, I save it locally.
